key_insight: Random projections let multi-copy quantum measurements be done on a smaller Hilbert space, trading coherent circuit complexity for extra sample copies.
engineering_relevance: This makes nonlinear state-property estimation more feasible on near-term hardware by matching the required quantum coherence to device limits.
method: Project the n-qubit state into a q-qubit subspace using random Haar-like projections.
Perform the collective multi-copy measurement on the reduced subspace instead of the full system.
Use derived Haar-averaged formulas to recover multivariate traces and quantify the copy overhead.
evidence_signal: The abstract derives explicit scaling laws showing that estimating tr(ρ^K) after reducing from n to q qubits needs about O(2^((n-q)(K-1))) copies.
watch_item: The benefit comes with rapidly growing sampling cost as more qubits are projected out, which can make large reductions impractical for higher K.
paper_title: Random Projections for Multi-Copy Quantum Algorithms
